concept.tagline: Grouping concurrent inference requests via dynamic or continuous iteration-level batching to keep GPUs compute-bound.
concept.purpose: Understand arithmetic intensity on GPUs, dynamic batching vs continuous iteration-level batching, and how to avoid Head-of-Line blocking and prefill-decode interference.

spark.summary: Group concurrent inference requests into tensor batches on the GPU to shift workloads from memory-bandwidth-bound to compute-bound without blowing tail latency.
spark.keyTakeaway: Use dynamic batching with a tight queue timeout (2–10 ms) for fixed-shape encoders, and iteration-level continuous batching with PagedAttention for autoregressive LLMs.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Serving a neural network at batch size 1 leaves modern GPUs (A100/H100) 80–90% idle because streaming weights from HBM into SRAM dominates compute time.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Iteration-Level LLM Batching (Zero Head-of-Line Blocking) (PREFILL CHUNK -> DECODE STEP -> EOS EJECT); Prefix-Aware Router -> Continuous Batching Engine -> Paged KV HBM (Prefix Router -> vLLM Scheduler -> Paged KV Blocks -> Tensor Cores).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Match the batching scheduler to model architecture and TTFT/ITL SLOs. At scale, an L7 inference router uses **prefix-cache-aware consistent routing** to steer repeated system-prompt prefixes to the same vLLM replica (maximizing RadixAttention/APC.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore PagedAttention, speculative decoding, FlashAttention, and quantization.

learningJourney.title: What is GPU Inference Batching
learningJourney.explanation:
Serving a neural network at batch size 1 leaves modern GPUs (A100/H100) 80–90% idle because streaming weights from HBM into SRAM dominates compute time.

**Batching** amortizes one HBM weight read across $B$ inputs, raising **arithmetic intensity (FLOPs/byte)** toward the GPU's roofline and multiplying throughput 5–20x per GPU.

sectionDiagram.title: Iteration-Level LLM Batching (Zero Head-of-Line Blocking)
sectionDiagram.summary: Unlike static request-level batching, continuous batching ejects finished sequences on every token step.

learningJourney.title: Why Static Batching causes Head-of-Line Blocking & Decode Stutter
learningJourney.explanation:
Two failure modes wreck tail latency in naive GPU servers:
- **Head-of-Line (HoL) Blocking**: in static request-level batches, one 4,096-token generation stalls 15 already-finished 64-token requests, spiking p99 10x.
- **Prefill-Decode Interference**: a 16k-token prompt prefill hogs GPU SMs for 400 ms, causing visible streaming stutter (`ITL > 200 ms`) for all active decode users.

ideas.title: Chunked Prefill
ideas.description: Split long 16k prefills into 512-token chunks interleaved with decode steps to keep inter-token latency smooth.

ideas.title: Length Bucketing / Ragged Tensors
ideas.description: Avoid wasting FLOPs on zero-padding by bucketing sequence lengths or using packed/ragged attention kernels.

learningJourney.title: Where GPU Batching applies (and where batch=1 wins)
learningJourney.explanation: Batching pays off when concurrent requests overlap within a 2–15 ms window.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: High-Concurrency Encoders & LLMs (>20 RPS)
benefits: 5–20x GPU throughput gain with sub-10 ms queue windows or continuous iteration batching.
costs: Requires PagedAttention KV-cache block management for LLMs.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Ultra-Low Traffic (<2 RPS) or <5ms Hard Real-Time
benefits: Execute immediately at batch=1 so requests never wait for an empty batch timer.
costs: Waiting for a queue timeout adds pure latency with zero batch formation.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: Dynamic Batching (Triton) & Continuous Batching (vLLM)
learningJourney.explanation: Set tight `max_queue_delay_microseconds` (2–10 ms) for encoders in Triton, and enable `enable_chunked_prefill` + `max_num_batched_tokens` in vLLM for LLMs.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```protobuf
# NVIDIA Triton config.pbtxt for fixed-shape embedding/vision encoders
dynamic_batching {
  preferred_batch_size: [ 8, 16, 32 ]
  max_queue_delay_microseconds: 5000  # 5 ms ceiling on queue wait
}
```

```bash
# vLLM continuous batching with chunked prefill to protect decode ITL
vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --max-num-seqs 128
```

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Dynamic Request Batching vs. Continuous Batching vs. Disaggregated P/D
learningJourney.explanation: Match the batching scheduler to model architecture and TTFT/ITL SLOs.

benefits: Simple to configure for fixed-compute encoders, embeddings, and vision models.
costs: Causes severe HoL blocking on variable-length autoregressive LLMs.

benefits: Zero HoL blocking; high KV-cache memory utilization via 16-token pages.
costs: Complex block-table scheduler; long prefills still contend with decodes unless chunked.

benefits: Eliminates prefill-decode interference completely by isolating compute-bound prefill from bandwidth-bound decode.
costs: Requires fast RDMA/NVLink KV-cache transfer between prefill and decode GPUs.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: KV-Cache Aware Router + Continuous Batching Pool
learningJourney.explanation: At scale, an L7 inference router uses **prefix-cache-aware consistent routing** to steer repeated system-prompt prefixes to the same vLLM replica (maximizing RadixAttention/APC KV-cache hits) while shedding load when GPU KV-cache utilization exceeds 90%.

sectionDiagram.title: Prefix-Aware Router -> Continuous Batching Engine -> Paged KV HBM

cards.label: 1. Prefix Affinity
cards.detail: Routing identical system prompts to the same replica reuses cached KV blocks.

cards.label: 2. KV Backpressure
cards.detail: Reject or queue at the gateway when KV-cache occupancy > 90% to avoid preemption thrashing.

cards.label: 3. Smooth ITL
cards.detail: Chunked prefill bounds inter-token latency even when 16k-token prompts arrive.

sectionDiagram.summary: Prefix routing + chunked continuous batching maximizes GPU arithmetic intensity without sacrificing streaming smoothness.

knowledgeCheck.question: How does continuous (iteration-level) batching eliminate Head-of-Line blocking compared to static request-level batching?

options.text: It forces every request to generate the exact same number of tokens
options.feedback: Output lengths remain variable; the scheduler adapts at each token step.

options.text: It schedules at the token-iteration level, immediately ejecting sequences on EOS and admitting queued requests without waiting for the longest sequence
options.feedback: Correct: short responses exit immediately and free KV-cache slots for new requests on the very next decode step.

options.text: It runs all requests at batch size 1
options.feedback: Batch size 1 leaves the GPU HBM-bandwidth bound.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
